name: unshare-then-netlink-xfrm
why: unshare(CLONE_NEWNET) then socket(AF_NETLINK, NETLINK_XFRM) (a0=0x10, a2=6) in the same pid within 10s is the DirtyFrag xfrm setup correlation
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for dirtyfrag_xfrm_behavioral.c (CLONE_NEWUSER then CLONE_NEWNET unshare, then NETLINK_XFRM socket)

name: unshare-combined-exact-then-netlink-xfrm
why: a single combined unshare whose a0 is exactly 0x50000000 (CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET, no other bits) then the NETLINK_XFRM socket fires, because the rule's a0|contains '50000000' is a substring match that this exact value satisfies. NOTE: this is a brittle substring test -- any extra namespace bit (unshare -Urnm = 0x50020000, or |NEWIPC = 0x58000000) does NOT contain '50000000' or '40000000' and so does NOT fire. Rule defect, tracked in detections/RULE_DEFECTS.md, entry L3: the CLONE_NEWNET bit should be matched robustly, not by hex substring
source: synthetic: an exploit issuing one unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET) == 0x50000000 then the xfrm socket

name: ip-netns-add-then-netlink-route
why: `ip netns add` unshares a network namespace (CLONE_NEWNET, a0=0x40000000) and opens a NETLINK_ROUTE socket (a2=0) for link setup; it keeps the unshare+netlink surface but the NETLINK_ROUTE protocol (a2=0, not NETLINK_XFRM a2=6) breaks the XFRM discriminator
source: recorded: strace of iproute2 6.1.0 `ip netns add` -- unshare(CLONE_NEWNET=0x40000000) and socket(AF_NETLINK, SOCK_RAW|SOCK_CLOEXEC, NETLINK_ROUTE=0)

name: mount-unshare-then-netlink-xfrm
why: unshare(CLONE_NEWNS) (a0=0x20000, a mount namespace) then the NETLINK_XFRM socket keeps the unshare surface but breaks the user/net-namespace flag the base requires (0x20000 contains neither '40000000' nor '50000000')
source: synthetic: a service with PrivateMounts= unsharing only the mount namespace, then (synthetically) an xfrm socket

name: netlink-xfrm-only-no-unshare
why: an IPsec daemon opens a NETLINK_XFRM socket with no namespace unshare at all; half the correlation, so the unshare base must be required
source: synthetic: strongSwan charon managing xfrm policy

name: unshare-and-xfrm-different-pid
why: unshare(CLONE_NEWNET) in a parent and the NETLINK_XFRM socket in a forked child within 10s split the halves across pids; the pid group-by must enforce same-process
source: synthetic: a runtime that unshares in the parent and configures xfrm in a child

name: unshare-then-xfrm-too-late
why: the same pid unshares and opens the NETLINK_XFRM socket 40s apart, outside the 10s window; the timespan must bound the correlation
source: synthetic: a daemon that unshares at startup and manages xfrm long after
